parsed.explanation: Combined federal-state regime: federal entry, document and custody rules create documented risk of refusal, stranded travel, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, and severe abuse in immigration/prison custody, while the state currently permits identity-congruent restrooms, has a hate-crime aggravator, and courts have enjoined some measures. No execution or identity criminalisation is documented, and state facilities are not banned, lifting it above 0.25-tier regimes, but federal state threat-framing and custody abuse keep it well below 0.45-0.55 tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal X-markers stopped Feb 2025, new passports only M/F; Nov 2025 Supreme Court allowed restrictions. Visa cable: document discrepancy or doubt about sex mandates refusal and extra evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility. Trans travellers reported confiscated/blocked passports and detentions of neighbouring citizens; trans-athlete entry ban Feb 2025.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic, limited waivers possible. Passport policy challenged by civil-liberties suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs; other orders partly blocked/enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: State DL/birth-certificate marker bans affect residents directly, but federal passport/visa screening is the visitor-facing gateway; a discrepancy at the border can become refusal and a fraud inquiry regardless of state protections.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau from 2026 adopted forced hair-cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution for transgender inmates; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Bathroom-arrest example: 24 hours in men's ward after trespass charge (up to 60 days).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented visitor-specific custody protocol, consular or independent oversight remedy in dossier; bureau stopped reporting transgender prisoner numbers from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border discrepancy can escalate to refusal, detention, then birth-sex placement and hormone denial; custody harm is state-perpetrated, not merely societal, and efficient federal enforcement of hostile policy is exposure, not recourse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; state map shows many states ban such use, with some criminal trespass triggers. State bill Jan 2026 would ban in public schools/universities and birth-sex prison housing, but is not law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: In this state, as of April 2026 law places no restriction on restroom use matching gender identity; two cities protect by ordinance; proposals died since 2021; 2023 appellate injunction protected a student's school bathroom use.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State permission does not cancel federal facility, entry-screening or custody rules where federal actors control the encounter; federal-building access remains uncertain due to injunction status.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-transition surgery, blockers and hormones for under-18s, upheld Nov 2024; a trans visitor under 18 cannot obtain that care here. Federal order labels minors' care 'chemical and surgical mutilation', proposed rule would bar under-18 reimbursement, and custody hormone removal is documented.
care_services.protection: Adult care availability in state is not documented; several federal orders blocked/enjoined, and emergency-care protections are not documented. Not documented.
care_services.interaction: A minor traveller or guardian faces care denial even if adult companion can use facilities; custody placement can interrupt any ongoing medication.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy May 2026 prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice guidance uses 'radical gender ideology' as extremist viewpoint; order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition. 2025 poll: 66% support assigned-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism text says powers will not target mere disagreement; hate-crime statute covers gender identity nationally and state aggravator since 2019, but use is not documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing increases police/border discretion in treating gender nonconformity as fraud/security risk, interacting with entry and custody exposures.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-18 care ban applies to visitor; school bathroom bill not law but signals risk; state classroom/parent-notification law and federal teacher-prosecution order affect school settings. Trans-athlete entry ban could affect minor competitors.
minors_guardians.protection: 2023 injunction barred schools limiting bathroom use during litigation; no documented visitor-school enrolment protection. Not documented for short-stay guardians.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor is not a resident student, but care-seeking, school visits, sport entry or a parent/guardian complaint could trigger state/federal rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of anti-trans street violence, dating-app ambush or police extortion in this state in dossier. National bias statistics cited are mainly sexual-orientation share, not trans-specific prevalence. Status: not_documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime aggravator (2019) and federal hate-crime statute provide potential recourse; city/county employment ordinances exist. Enforcement frequency deliberately not counted.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Paper recourse may mitigate isolated incidents, but dossier does not show it operating for visitors, and cannot offset documented federal custody/border exposures.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies are slow/contested: passport suit unresolved, DL-ban challenge pending, several executive orders blocked/enjoined without clear current scope, legal-aid FAQ needed for document decisions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have issued injunctions (school bathroom 2023, care ban injunction 2023 then stay/upheld), suit pending, and existing X passports honoured until expiry.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty itself is traveller exposure: which federal measures are in effect at travel time determines entry/facility/care outcomes, and state remedies cannot bind federal border/custody actors.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in routine identity stops, confiscation and weak judicial remedy, but this case is lower (less safe) than 0.35-B because documented custody includes forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse and hormone removal, and border refusal can trigger permanent fraud ineligibility; no execution is documented.

Similar document-mismatch detention, humiliation and scarce/slow remedies, but this case sits below 0.45-A: federal custody abuse is documented as a pattern by the state itself, and the visa cable expressly contemplates lifetime ineligibility, whereas custodial sentences are described as unlikely in 0.45-A.

Much lower than 0.65-A: there, national equality law protected the visitor, release was reliably ordered, apology/compensation followed and no imprisonment occurred. Here federal policy itself restricts markers/facilities, courts allow restrictions to take effect, and remedies are pending or enjoined rather than reliably effective.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is federal-first: state permission for identity-congruent restrooms and a hate-crime aggravator do not pre-empt federal passport/visa screening, federal facilities, federal custody hormone removal, or immigration detention abuses. Probability of outing is driven by document discrepancy at entry and in federal settings; severity if outed ranges from refusal/stranding and possible lifetime ineligibility to birth-sex custody with documented abuse. No capital or general identity crime is documented, courts remain active, and the state layer is comparatively permissive, preventing a 0.25 rating. For a minor, the upheld under-18 care ban is an added documented exposure.
